newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures ends higher to limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures ends higher to limit up.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended higher to up as much as the daily limit of $10.00 per tbf after posting limit gains late. November expired lower on further liquidation, traders said.

January paced the limit advance late monring but eased on spread action to end up $6.50 per tbf at $403.90. March, May and distant September ended up the daily limit of $10.00. November expired earlier at $455.00, off $8.70 per tbf.
All but November ran up for a limit gain late monring on short covering and buy stops. The market appeared oversold after recent sharp losses and discount to cash, traders said.
"Those back months are oversold," one trader said.

But spreaders sold January and bought March and May late to pare January's gain. November remained under long liquidation pressure at expiration. Although many deliveries were seen in strong hands, speculative longs exited the market following an easier undertone to cash product, they said.
"Cash (trade) was real quiet and prices for spruce are $450 to $460 from what I'm hearing," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Demand for wood slackened amid recent high prices and the onset of winter weather, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $473 per tbf, down $7 from midweek and week ago levels, and some mills were accepting bids under this level.
Prudential Securities, Refco, LIT division of First Options, R.J. O'Brien and E.D.&F. Man bought January on the early advance, pit sources added.
